describes: A land recipe that opens a Datadog notebook to watch a merge's rollout, linked from the Lookout tab's Land stage. Its step writes to Datadog, so it is marked writes: the first landing waits for the person's approval, and an edit to the recipe asks again.
verify: With DD_API_KEY, DD_APP_KEY and DD_SITE set, run the notebook step by hand from the repo root with MERGE_SHA and PR set: it must print the new notebook's URL and exit 0, and the notebook must show in Datadog. Replace the cells with the queries your rollout should be watched by. Then set "verified": true here, with the date and the Datadog site in "verifiedAgainst".
needs: DD_API_KEY and DD_APP_KEY in the environment the app runs landings in (never in the recipe), and DD_SITE (datadoghq.com, datadoghq.eu, ...)
the queries that show your rollout: the cells below are a placeholder

recipe.name: a Datadog notebook watching the rollout

steps.run: body=$(jq -n --arg sha "$MERGE_SHA" --arg pr "$PR" '{data: {type: "notebooks", attributes: {name: ("Rollout of " + ($sha[0:7]) + (if $pr == "" then "" else " (PR #" + $pr + ")" end)), time: {live_span: "4h"}, cells: [{type: "notebook_cells", attributes: {definition: {type: "markdown", text: ("Watching the rollout of " + $sha + ". Replace this cell with the service's error rate and latency.")}}}]}}}') || exit 1; out=$(printf '%s' "$body" | curl -fsS -X POST "https://api.$DD_SITE/api/v1/notebooks" -H "DD-API-KEY: $DD_API_KEY" -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: $DD_APP_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @-) || exit 1; id=$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.data.id // empty') && [ -n "$id" ] || { echo 'Datadog made no notebook' >&2; exit 1; }; echo "https://app.$DD_SITE/notebook/$id"
steps.note: creates the notebook and prints its URL; fails unless Datadog answered with one. The keys come from the environment, never from this file
